claims.claim: Evagrius Ponticus was a Christian mystic and writer who lived from approximately 345 to 399 CE.
Evagrius was born in Ibora, Pontus, and died in Cellia in the Nitrian Desert, Egypt.
Evagrius was ordained a reader by Basil of Caesarea and later served as archdeacon under Gregory of Nazianzus in Constantinople, where he participated in the Second Ecumenical Council in 381.

After a personal spiritual crisis, Evagrius left Constantinople for Jerusalem, where he took monastic vows in 383 in the communities of Melania the Elder and Rufinus of Aquileia, before moving to Egypt.
The Tractatus ad Eulogium is an early work by Evagrius Ponticus.
The Tractatus ad Eulogium is addressed to Eulogius, a monk, as indicated by its Greek title 'ΛΟΓΟΣ ΠΡΟΣ ΕΥΛΟΓΙΟΝ ΜΟΝΑΧΟΝ' (Discourse to Eulogius the Monk).
The Tractatus ad Eulogium was transmitted under the name of Nilus of Ancyra (sub nomine Nili Ancyrani), a common attribution for Evagrian works.
A modern critical edition and French translation of the Tractatus ad Eulogium was published by Fogielman in 2017 as 'Évagre le Pontique. À Euloge, Les vices opposés aux vertus'.
Evagrius developed a meticulous taxonomy of evil thoughts, their origins, and associated physical experiences, arranging his works in an ascetic curriculum for training monks.
Evagrius's teachings were later considered unorthodox in some strands of late ancient Christianity, though the Armenian and Syrian churches continued to cherish his writings.
